statement_summary: One group program aligned to CSF 2.0 meeting the HIPAA Security Rule for every covered entity and business associate
Group CISO accountable; each covered entity and BDS designate their own security and privacy officials
Annual SP 800-30 risk analysis per division with roll-up to group
Risk acceptance authority by level; High risks that could delay response or harm patients must be treated
Division supplements may not weaken group policy; re-align within 90 days; annual attestation
Divisions document common control inheritance, including vehicle and center systems, and confirm it yearly
Proportionate sanctions documented by Privacy Officer and HR
No BAA, no PHI; client data not routed to new subcontractors or features without a contract check
Annual independent assessment of common controls and division samples
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
Six-year retention of security documentation
AI registration and approval before deployment, mode change, or material change
Confirm CJI status and agreements before any interface carries law enforcement data
Unique identities; shared accounts only by documented exception
Role-based least privilege; client agency users see only their own incidents
MFA for all workforce; phishing-resistant for administrators; badge plus PIN at consoles
Vendor access only through PAM with named accounts, approval, and recording
Disable access within 4 hours of termination; suspend idle per-diem accounts after 30 days
Quarterly certification including privileged, service, and vendor accounts
Just-in-time privileged access through PAM
Lockout, idle lock, and session limits; dispatch console equivalent measure
Sealed break-glass accounts for each critical system, tested quarterly
Every vehicle device inventoried, individually authenticated, and free of default passwords
Client agency users federate or use guest accounts with MFA
Report suspected incidents to the SOC within 1 hour
One group severity scale and group playbooks
Switch to manual dispatch at once; client and county calls within 15 minutes
regulatory_driver: County ambulance agreements; client dispatch contracts; C-EMERGENCY-R04 (164.308(a)(7)(ii)(C))

statement_summary: Record each entity's discovery date
Each covered entity decides its own notices; BDS and corporate notify per BAA and 164.410
Counsel maintains the multi-party matrix and notice register; approves external notices
Severity 1 to the disclosure committee within 24 hours; Form 8-K within 4 business days of a materiality determination
Ransom payments need board approval, counsel, insurer, and an OFAC check
Annual cross-division exercise with a CAD outage, the matrix, and a materiality decision
Preserve evidence with chain of custody; legal hold on logs
Lessons learned within 30 days; update registers and POA&M
Four classes; call audio and card data are Restricted
Encrypt Restricted information at rest and in transit
Client data in client partitions; used only as each BAA permits
Interface register with permitted fields; filter everything else
No card numbers spoken to agents or stored in recordings
Immutable, separate backups; quarterly restore tests for High-criticality systems
Sanitize or destroy media with a certificate
Records schedule (CAD 7 years; state EMS and Medicare periods; file transfer copies 14 days)
No Restricted information in unapproved AI tools
Job-need access only; no personal CAD or record searches
Annual training, monthly reminders, quarterly phishing exercises
Role training for telecommunicators and fleet technicians
Restricted information only on managed devices; no personal phone photos
Approved generative AI tools only
Recording only after the consent state law requires
